Regulations should prioritize waste prevention, durability, repair and reuse—not recycling alone—and set measurable outcomes with credible enforcement. Include workers and waste handlers in policy design, protect labor rights, phase in requirements with support for smaller suppliers, and coordinate across markets to limit loopholes and shifted costs. These measures can help circular practices take hold, but results depend on implementation and monitoring.
